key_insight: In Huntington’s disease trial analyses, prognostic covariate adjustment increased statistical power from 80% to up to 90% at fixed sample size, or reduced required sample size by 15–28% versus no adjustment.
clinical_relevance: These findings could support more efficient Huntington’s disease trials; this study concerns trial methodology, not cancer drug discovery or treatment efficacy.
method: Trained nine algorithms using 16 baseline covariates to predict progression across five UHDRS endpoints.
Developed a minimal six-covariate linear model for Total Functional Capacity (TFC).
Evaluated predictions and efficiency gains using an independent trial placebo arm.
evidence_signal: Models were trained on 16,398 Enroll-HD participants and tested on 260 GENERATION-HD1 placebo participants; nonlinear models showed no performance advantage over linear-based models.
watch_item: Evaluation in a single trial placebo arm leaves generalizability to other trial populations and settings uncertain.
paper_title: Quantifying statistical power gains from prognostic modeling in Huntington's Disease
